x1vnvait.author: Plato
x1vnvait.label: Two strips joined like the letter X: the Same and the Other
x1vnvait.translation: This entire compound he divided lengthways into two parts, which he joined to one another at the centre like the letter X, and bent them into a circular form, connecting them with themselves and each other at the point opposite to their original meeting-point; ... Now the motion of the outer circle he called the motion of the same, and the motion of the inner circle the motion of the other or diverse.
x1vnvait.reading: The Demiurge splits the soul-mixture into two strips "like Christmas koulourakia" joined in a χ. In the world soul and in ours, the circle of the Same matches the celestial equator and the circle of the Other the ecliptic. At an equinox the circles meet (inner balance); at a solstice they are farthest apart.
